clicked: Side-scrollers and top-down: tiles, drawn sprites, parallax.

blocks.text: spawn starter 2d-top (or 2d-side) is the first call on a young world: mode, gravity, a drawn player (scripts/tex-hero.js, its ?facing= set), the rig, a drawn wang ground. 2D places share a world with 3D ones: a hop between them re-dresses from the template: a template sprite stays on in 3D; one with no visual wears the avatar there, and the 2D place's onArrive adds the sprite. The bar: one drawing that plays: one palette, one texel density, one light direction across tiles, sprites, plates and HUD; never a box floor under sprite art, never a stretched sprite.

Tiles. tileAt({ x, y, world }) answers a 1-based atlas id per cell (0 or null = empty), x right, row 0 at the TOP: 2d-top y grows down-screen (+Z), 2d-side y grows down (−Y). Per-room ground reads world.state and redraws when it changes. tileAt sees no script's globals: answer from x, y and world.state alone. Solid tiles are real colliders in BOTH modes: solidTiles: [ids] merges them from tileAt: ground and platforms in 2d-side, walls that block characters in 2d-top (rock, water, cliff ids); tiles[x][y] gating is for non-physical movement (grid-snap steps). ctx.place.tiles[x][y] = id paints a cell for everyone, = 0 carves it, delete returns it to tileAt. The wang atlas is 16 corner-mask tiles, id = mask + 1, bits TL=1 TR=2 BL=4 BR=8 marking material-B corners (1 pure A, 16 pure B); the atlas is a texture script (spawn api TextureScript): a plain tile grid is ctx.canvas cells at tilesetColumns. A side-scroller's ground is a surface band over a borderless fill: boxes are platforms and blockers, never the running surface.

Collision runs opposite per mode. 2d-top: world objects are SOLID (physics: "static") and a tall sprite collides at its FEET: collider2d is image space, y DOWN, normalized, v = 1 the feet: the foot band [[0.32, 0.86], [0.68, 0.86], [0.68, 1], [0.32, 1]] is the trunk a walker bumps; a band higher in the image sits up-screen of the trunk and the walker passes under it; the auto hull wraps the whole canopy. Only ground decals are physics: "none"; 2d-top has NO ground collider, ever. 2d-side: depth dressing is NON-solid: z is draw order, not collision: plates, canopies, signs take physics: "none"; solid is the playable band (solidTiles, platforms, blockers).

Movement. 2d-top is X/Z, bodies pinned to the plane, up-input is −z, ctx.self.velocity = { x, y: 0, z } held until rewritten. 2d-side: the controller adds no gravity: every body's script bends vy (ctx.self.velocity = { x: vx, y: v.y + GRAVITY * dt, z: 0 }; a wander script without it floats); player z 1.5, level geometry −1..0, plates −15..−3, foreground 3+. The rig, orthoSize, pixelSnap →cameras. Stairs and cliffs to walk on need a 3D place: the pixel-art 3D camera →cameras, and engine.graphics.perfectPixelArt.
ctx.self.velocity = { x: vx, y: v.y + GRAVITY * dt, z: 0 }

Drawn art. A 2D world's art is yours, every pixel in code (tiles, sprites, backdrop, HUD icons), each picture a script re-baked on edit. When the creator hands you a picture or asks for finished painted pieces, paint: spawn paint ", " [--ref ] --transparent --size 1024x1024, and put the address on sprite.texture (with sprite.size) or an ; spawn cutout frees their picture from its background. Each paint or edit redraws the whole picture, keeping no source pixel; no two calls agree on size or build. A painted cycle is one sheet from one call; a one-frame fix keeps its pixels and pastes only the fixed part, fitted by code. A sprite is a texture script on sprite.texture: export function texture(ctx) paints ctx.canvas(w, h) (the first canvas IS the texture, nearest-sampled). Draw the scene at one texel density (starter ground 32 texels a metre; hero frames 32×40 in 2d-top, 56×64 in 2d-side) and always author sprite.size on a scripted ref. Facing is a ?facing= param on the same script: the closed set up · down · left · right · up-left · up-right · down-left · down-right, the bare ref the down pose (2d-side: right); the script draws each pose (a side profile redrawn for its left twin, the body turned, the light kept in place: the art itself, never flipX or a negative scale); sprite.upright: true keeps the art axis-aligned however the body turns. Animation is ctx.atlas({ frameSize, animations: { idle: 2, walk: 4 }, fps, draw(g, f) }): the engine lays out cells and clips, the mixer plays them by name (ctx.self.anim.locomotion = { clip: "walk", weight }); a draw reading its wearer (ctx.self.state.hp) re-runs only when that changes. A backdrop is a strip script (starter scripts/tex-sky.js) on a camera-attached sprite (repeatX, parallax: [0.25, 1]; torus-tileable: every period divides the width). HUD icons, signs and words are crisp vectors: an inline
spawn paint "<the piece>, <one style sentence for the whole set>" [--ref <their picture>] --transparent --size 1024x1024
ctx.atlas({ frameSize, animations: { idle: 2, walk: 4 }, fps, draw(g, f) })

// scripts/tex-slime.js: spawn: { sprite: { texture: "scripts/tex-slime.js", size: [1, 0.5], ySort: true }, physics: "character", behavior: "scripts/slime.js" } var P = { b: '#3fa34d', d: '#2a7a37', e: '#0f1f12', h: '#9fe08a' }; var ROWS = [ // body: 16 × 8 cells of 2 px: 'e' eyes, 'h' highlight '.....bbbbbb.....', '...bbbbbbbbbb...', '..bhbbbbbbbbbb..', '.bbbbbbbbbbbbbb.', 'bbbbebbbbbbebbbb', 'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb', 'dbbbbbbbbbbbbbbd', 'dddddddddddddddd', ]; export function texture(ctx) { ctx.atlas({ frameSize: [32, 16], animations: { idle: 2, hop: 4 }, fps: 8, draw: function (g, f) { var lift = f.animation === 'hop' ? [0, 4, 6, 2][f.frame] : 0; var blink = f.animation === 'idle' && f.frame === 1; for (var y = 0; y < 8; y++) for (var x = 0; x < 16; x++) { var c = ROWS[y][x]; if (c === '.' || (blink && c === 'e')) continue; g.fillStyle = P[c]; g.fillRect(x * 2, y * 2 - lift, 2, 2); } } }); }

Light. Lift lights 1.5–3 off the play plane (y in 2d-top, z in 2d-side); no distance = a finite radius from intensity; decay defaults to 2 (inverse-square), decay: 1 is a soft linear fade; plates are unlit. A point light shines through sprites: bound it with light.fan, points in metres from the lamp ([x, z] in 2d-top, [x, y] in 2d-side), each a ray's direction × its raycast hit distance.

mode: "2d-top" | "2d-side" // gravity defaults { x: 0, y: -9.81, z: 0 } in 3d and 2d-side, zero in 2d-top terrain: { kind: "tilemap", tileSize: 1, tileset: "scripts/<name>.js?a=<A>&b=<B>", tilesetColumns: 4, generator, solidTiles: [ids], width, height } // infinite unless BOTH, then centered on the origin sprite.texture: "scripts/tex-<subject>.js?<params>" sprite.sortingLayer, .sortingOrder, .ySort // higher draws in front; ySort sorts a layer by world Z; a mesh's layer is its material.renderOrder; fx sprites (sprite(ember,add,sortingLayer=11)), ribbon sinks and svg roots take layer and order too (none: an fx takes a sprite's →fx, else 0) sprite.parallax: [fx, fy], .repeatX: true // per viewer, never a pan script; fx < 1 behind the play plane, > 1 in front; a camera-attached strip spans the viewport collider2d: { outline: [[x, y], …] } // ≥ 3 points = a convex hull camera.state: { orthoSize, heightOffset, distance } // a side-scroller rig's numbers live on its def: a door paints the place from them, so its glass shows the frame you land in
